children: European governments are set to choose between two experienced and pragmatic economists from Spain and the Netherlands to succeed Christine Lagarde, who is stepping down as head of the European Central Bank in February.
A group of finance ministers from the 21 members of the eurozone said Friday that it had received two nominations for the job: Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos and Klaas Knot from the Netherlands.

The candidates will be considered by the Eurogroup at a meeting Monday, before European Union leaders make the final choice. They next meet on Nov. 13, but that might be a little early to make a final call, since leaders are obliged to consult with the European Parliament and the ECB's governing council before reaching a decision.

The successful candidate will take over an institution that is facing a jump in inflation as a result of the higher energy prices that have accompanied the war between the U.S. and Iran, and has already raised its key interest rate twice this year.

While the eurozone economy has grown more strongly than expected when the war began, it remains sluggish and beset by challenges, ranging from more intense competition from China in automobiles and other sophisticated manufacturing sectors, to the fraying of its economic relationship with the U.S. under President Trump.

Closer to home, a sharp rise in yields on French government bonds carries as yet faint echoes of the eurozone's debt crisis of the last decade, and the new ECB president might be faced with some difficult decisions about how to respond if that threatens to raise borrowing costs for other parts of the currency area.

Spain's government nominated Hernandez de Cos, general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, whom former colleagues describe as a technical whiz with a strong grasp of central banking and monetary policy.  Hernandez de Cos was governor of the Bank of Spain from 2018 to 2024, during which time he helped set eurozone interest rates as a member of the ECB's governing council.

"Pablo Hernandez de Cos is an exceptional candidate, with a renowned  international prestige and a track record that demonstrates leadership, independence and the ability to engage in dialogue," Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo wrote in his nomination letter.

The Dutch government nominated Klaas Knot, one of Europe's longest-serving central bank governors before he stepped down last year. He therefore has long experience in setting interest rates for the eurozone.  While holding that job, he also served as head of the Group of 20's Financial Stability Board.

The Rolling Stones-loving economist gained a reputation as a monetary-policy hawk during the eurozone debt crisis. But Knot's position softened over time and he is now seen as a middle-of-the-road pragmatist who would be more responsive to bond-market tremors than earlier in his career.

While competence matters in choosing the head of the ECB and other European institutions, so too does nationality, with governments keen to see their citizens wielding power and influence in areas of importance to them. The ECB's founding president was Dutch, while a Spanish national has never held the post, although Luis de Guindos served as vice president until earlier this year.

Two other senior roles at the ECB are also opening up in the coming months. Germany's Isabel Schnabel is stepping down early as the executive board member responsible for markets, while Ireland's Philip Lane is soon to leave his position as chief economist. Settling on a three-job package is likely to involve some  horse-trading.

One potential obstacle for Hernandez de Cos is the Nov. 29 election in Spain that could result in defeat for the left-of-center government that has nominated him. However, the country's main opposition has declared its support for his candidacy.
